born.why: This code improves survival by distinguishing between critical and moderate danger, allowing engagement with items when risk is acceptable, while using past performance (if available) to avoid recurring high-risk choices.

The code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding high-risk item traits (>80) unless the default is already safe, and uses history to reject defaults that previously led to critical n1 levels, while approach ensures engagement only when current risk is low.

This code aggressively prioritizes survival by treating the gray zone (60-80 n1) as a warning stage where safety (a4) is preferred if instability (pending debt) is detected, and lowers the approach threshold to ensure the agent only moves when truly safe, minimizing long-term n1 creep.

The code prioritizes survival by rejecting items with high relative health costs (risk > 20) when not in default mode, and enforces a hard stop near death (n1 >= 95) to preserve state, while trusting the historical default choice when risks are manageable.

The code prioritizes survival by strictly retreating (a4) when n1 exceeds safe thresholds or when pending loss indicates instability, while allowing the agent to act on its default preference only when n1 is low and financial state is stable.

It shifts focus from a static `n1` threshold to a dynamic risk model using `n2` (pending cost), allowing aggressive action when safe and conservative idling when the immediate threat is high, thus optimizing survival time by balancing gain against real-time exposure.

The code tightens the safety thresholds for both deciding and approaching, prioritizing survival over potential gains by reverting to the safe option 'a4' more aggressively when risk levels rise or pending debt is detected.
